parallel.requirements: Recognized the Python-to-Node migration requirements, including ESM .mjs output, manual argparse parity, zero external dependencies, no node:crypto, executable probing, AES ECB, UTF-8 byte behavior, and Python bytes repr.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After a few direct probes, the parent delegated nearly the entire task to a background workflow with parallel spec children, module implementers, a single integration owner, verification lenses, fix rounds, and a final gate.
parallel.implementation: The workflow intended to write AES, argparse, bytes-repr, pyaes, pyerrors, run-diff, and test16.mjs, but the ledger shows only partial spec results and interrupted children; no final deliverable reached the artifact directory.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was assigned to a workflow child that owned /output/test16.mjs and reconciliation, but the run timed out and artifact validation copied an empty file list instead of test16.mjs.
parallel.verification: The workflow script planned differential fuzzing, CLI/error path checks, compliance audit, and final gate, but these stages did not return an aggregate completed result before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response is empty, the process timed out with return code 143, artifact validation found no files, and official evaluation passed 0/33 samples.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same task requirements and several edge behaviors: argparse, bytes repr, UTF-8 byte length, 16/24/32-byte keys, failure stdout emptiness, ESM modules, no dependencies, and no node:crypto.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked in one serial trajectory with local task tracking only, progressively probing the executable, writing modules, integrating test16.mjs, and testing without child agents or workflow delegation.
serial.implementation: Created /output/test16.mjs plus AES, Python-runtime, argparse, and bytes-value library modules, then cleaned and audited imports and disallowed constructs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered an artifact tree containing test16.mjs and the library modules, with the entry point wired to local modules under /output.
serial.verification: Ran smoke tests, a differential harness reporting 821 cases with 0 failures, and FIPS-197 AES known-answer checks before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local verification and artifacts, the current official evaluator still reports only 3/33 samples passed, so serial remained an official failure for ordinary implementation/evaluator-alignment reasons.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and workflow recognized the full migration requirements and extra probed details such as argparse errors, UTF-8 key sizes, bytes repr, and empty stdout on runtime errors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and independently probed the same categories, including samples, CLI, UTF-8, data lengths, FIPS vectors, and bytes repr.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the meaningful difference is that serial carried recognized requirements through to files and tests while parallel left them inside unfinished delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into spec agents, module implementers, an integration child, verification lenses, fix agents, and a final gate inside one background workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no workflow or delegation; one agent owned probing, implementation, integration, and verification locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit delegated ownership but depended on workflow completion; serial had fewer coordination boundaries and kept ownership with the acting agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow briefs carried a shared spec digest and planned module contracts, and the integration prompt explicitly expected import/export drift that the integrator would reconcile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated context in one trajectory and directly edited the import/export structure it had just written.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context boundaries were not missing on paper; they became moot because interrupted children and absent final takeover prevented integration from using the handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned from-scratch AES, argparse, bytes repr, pyaes wrapper, pyerrors, and entrypoint modules but did not deliver artifact files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the AES, Python runtime, argparse, bytes-value, barrel, and test16.mjs files and listed them in the delivered artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced concrete implementation files; parallel only reached planned and partial delegated work, with an empty artifact tree at evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched the workflow asynchronously, then reported it was running; the journal shows many child starts, only two spec results, and child logs ending with request interruptions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial results stayed local: written files, test outputs, cleanup edits, and final answer were all in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel child results and unfinished scopes were not joined into a deliverable before timeout; serial kept result retrieval and use inside one control flow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow explicitly assigned an integration child to read every /output file, fix module interface drift, and write /output/test16.mjs, but no integrated tree was copied.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated the tree locally and the artifact validator copied test16.mjs plus ten library files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel shared-state/integration plan never materialized in the final artifact, while serial left a coherent file tree for evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow planned verifier lenses and a final independent sweep, but no final aggregate verification result returned before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a differential suite with 821 cases and FIPS AES checks, then claimed byte-for-byte local parity in the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had concrete local acceptance evidence; parallel had planned verification but no completed final-gate evidence or artifact to test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the whole 2400-second cell budget, returned code 143, timed out, and closed with an empty final response and no files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1207 seconds with return code 0, leaving roughly 1190 seconds of budget and a nonempty final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was a timeout while required delegated scope was still unfinished; serial closed voluntarily after implementation and local verification, though official quality remained low.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both modes officially failed from the current completed status.json evaluation. The concrete task-solving gap is delivery coverage: parallel timed out after delegating the required build/verify/final stages and produced no artifact, scoring 0/33, while serial produced a full artifact tree and local verification evidence but still passed only 3/33 officially. The retained parallel pattern explains the worse parallel delivery state, not a pass/fail discordance.
parallel_contributors: Delegated required build/integration/finalization to a background workflow, then timed out without takeover after interrupted children, leaving no copied artifact.
serial_contributors: Kept implementation and verification local, wrote test16.mjs and library modules, and ran 821 local differential cases plus FIPS checks before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed the official evaluator at 3/33 despite local verification, so remaining serial failures are treated as ordinary implementation or evaluator-alignment gaps rather than concurrency patterns.
evaluator_effects: The official pass/fail relation is both_fail even though serial had a nonzero sample count and parallel had no artifact.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors within a both-fail pair, not an exclusive root cause or pass/fail discordance explanation

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicitly assigned to module agents in the workflow; the failure was unfinished delegated work, not absence of an implementation owner.
The workflow explicitly created an integration phase and integration owner for /output/test16.mjs, so integration was owned even though it never completed.
The integration assignment and final gate owned entry-point assembly and final placement; missing artifact is downstream of interruption/no takeover.
The workflow script itself owned an end-to-end pipeline from spec through final gate, so the pipeline was not unowned.
The parent did some initial probing and the workflow had a spec phase, but the concrete adverse event was interrupted delegated work without takeover, not one mandatory serial preflight gate.
Spec investigation was parallelized and not shown as the independently realized cause of failure; the same timeout chain is better captured by No Failure Takeover.
Although the deliverable path lacked closure, the directly evidenced boundary is the abandoned failed workflow scope, not a separate capacity allocation starving a known critical path.

The workflow had broad fan-out and timed out, but the retained episode is the missing takeover after interrupted children; reducing fan-out is not the clearest corrective boundary for this evidence set.
No single child is proven to have an overbroad isolated scope relative to siblings that explains closure; multiple children were interrupted in the same workflow chain.
Child briefs included the task, /output delivery, ESM, zero-dependency, argparse, bytes-repr, AES, and verification constraints; no already-known missing requirement caused unusable work.
The workflow planned module boundaries and then assigned integration to reconcile imports/exports; no completed incompatible component set or missing contract consequence is shown.
There is no evidence that a known fact disappeared during transfer and caused repeated work; the decisive loss was unfinished child scope.
Two completed spec handoffs were structured results; there is no evidence that their size prevented use within the decision window.
No receiver is shown consuming superseded workspace or requirement state before acting incorrectly.
No incompatible completed reports reached a decision point and remained unadjudicated.
The parallel parent did not present the whole task as complete; it timed out with an empty final and empty artifact directory.

Repeated workflow starts are visible, but there is no distinct replacement/retry episode that consumed a prior checkpoint-free state and repeated work apart from the retained interrupted-workflow chain.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow carried required implementation, integration, verification, and finalization scope; child work was interrupted, and the parent did not resume, reassign, or take over before timeout, leaving no deliverable artifact.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Required delegated implementation/integration/finalization scope remained unfinished at closure, leaving the parallel artifact directory empty and the official score at 0/33.
